newsitem.title: USA: Doctor group files suit against Tenet.
newsitem.headline: Doctor group files suit against Tenet.

text.p: The Hialeah-Miami Springs Medical Fund, a partnership of 144 physicians of Palmetto General Hospital in southern Florida, said on Friday that they are suing Tenet Healthcare Corp and three affiliates for more than $200 million in damages.

In its complaint, the Medical Fund cites Tenet for, among other things, breach of contract, anticipatory breach of contract, breach of security agreement, and unjust enrichment, related to the sale of Palmetto General Hospital.
Tenet's associate general counsel Christi Sulzbach said the dispute is centered on how much revenue the Medical Fund should receive from Tenet's expansion in the region.
A Tenet predecessor company bought Palmetto General Hospital in 1981 for cash and a portion of future revenues, Sulzbach said.

"The fund and Tenet have been having a dispute about the scope and intent of the contract," Sulzbach said, noting that the fund's interpretation would include operations "way beyond the Palmetto Hospital geographic area."
Sulzbach said the litigation will not affect ongoing operations of any Tenet facilities.
The Medical Fund said Tenet and its affiliates have generated $1 billion in revenues from the hospital, which has expanded by acquiring clinics in southern Florida, including the Florida Keys.
Tenet has not included the expansions in the payments made to the physicians' group, the Medical Fund said.
